html:
The war fought across the former Russian Empire after the Russian Revolution, from late 1917 to 1922, in which the Bolsheviks (the Reds) beat a mix of enemies and built the Soviet state.

The Reds, led by Vladimir Lenin, held the central core around Moscow and Petrograd, with its railways and factories. Leon Trotsky built the Red Army from scratch. Against them stood the Whites, a loose set of former tsarist officers, liberals and moderate socialists, under generals such as Kolchak in Siberia, Denikin and then Wrangel in the south, and Yudenich near Petrograd. Britain, France, the United States and Japan sent troops and supplies to the Whites. Peasant armies, anarchists and national movements in Ukraine, the Caucasus and Central Asia fought on their own account, and Poland, Finland and the Baltic states won independence.

The Whites never agreed on a goal and were spread around the edges. By late 1920 the last of them had left Crimea. In the far east Moscow ran the Far Eastern Republic as a buffer state while Japanese troops stayed in Siberia. When they left, the Reds took Vladivostok in October 1922. The Soviet Union was founded that December.

Both sides used terror. The Reds took grain by force under "War Communism", and the famine of 1921 and the Kazakh famine followed. With fighting, disease and hunger, the war cost millions of lives, and over a million people fled abroad.
sum: The war fought across the former Russian Empire after the Russian Revolution, from late 1917 to 1922, in which the Bolsheviks (the Reds) beat a mix of enemies and built the Soviet state.
